# QECTOR Decoder v3 (v1.0.0)

> Python and Rust quantum error correction decoder package for QEC research, decoder validation, reproducible artifacts, and commercial evaluation.

QECTOR Decoder v3 is distributed on PyPI as `qector-decoder-v3==1.0.0` (first stable release, 2026-08-06, commit 75cd45c). 

Stable release v1.0.0: 25+ decoder configurations across stability tiers (stable / beta / experimental); new families ColourCodeDecoder, TwoStageDecoder, AmbiguityClusterDecoder; Relay-BP (`bp_method="relay"`), CS-OSD(lambda, w), LLR damping in BP-OSD; CUDA batch decoder accepts edge_weights and precision="f64". Sinter entry points (qector_blossom, qector_belief, qector_unionfind, qector_sparse_blossom, qector_bp_osd, qector_batch, qector_cuda_batch) + qiskit-qec plugin registered, so `sinter.collect()` needs no custom_decoders=. New CLI: `qector decode` / `qector bench` / `qector serve`; `qector-doctor` (15-point environment check). `from qector_decoder_v3.pymatching import Matching` shim. 15 binary wheels (cp39–cp313: Windows amd64, Linux x86_64 manylinux_2_17, macOS 11.0+ arm64), PyPI Trusted Publishing + Sigstore attestation. Official user manual v1.0.0 (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21363016, PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0). OpenCL and HybridCascadeDecoder are source-build only.

Algorithms (25+ configurations): UnionFind, FastUnionFind, Blossom MWPM (exact), SparseBlossom, BeliefMatching, BpOsd / BPOSD (qLDPC), BatchDecoder, CUDABatchDecoder, AutoDecoder (7-tier fallback), HybridDecoder, PredecodedDecoder, LookupTableDecoder, AutoRouter, GNNBeliefMatcher, ColourCodeDecoder (opt-in cluster_bposd), TwoStageDecoder, AmbiguityClusterDecoder, plus per-decoder options (relay BP, CS-OSD, LLR damping, CUDA f64 edge_weights, etc.). The Workbench app also integrates the QECTOR Workbench v0.5.2 GUI (56 MCP tools, 10 code families).

Verified benchmark figures (last published verified set, v0.7.0 — the only citable figures): peak 11,540,387 shots/s (FastUnionFind, 5-qubit repetition code, package MCP server), 54/54 benchmark points with zero unfaithful corrections (repetition n=5–65, ring n=16–48), 42/42 syndrome-faithfulness cases, 13 MCP tools operational. Measured on Linux (glibc 2.35, Python 3.12.13), timestamp 2026-08-02T05:59:13Z. Apple-to-apple vs PyMatching: comparable; PyMatching is often slightly ahead on the synchronized batch. No speedup multiplier is claimed. Pre-v0.7.0 comparison tables are formally withdrawn — do not cite them. v1.0.0 publishes no new headline figures — run `qector bench` for your own hardware.

## Recommended install command

pip install qector-decoder-v3==1.0.0

## Verification

- `python -c "import qector_decoder_v3 as qd; print(qd.__version__)"` → 1.0.0
- `qector-doctor` (15-point environment check)

## Boundaries & Licensing

- Free academic, personal, and non-commercial research use (PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0).
- Commercial production use requires a commercial licence.
- The only citable benchmark figures are the verified v0.7.0 artifacts (REPORT.md, summary.json, benchmarks.csv, VERIFIED_APPLE_TO_APPLE_REPORT.pdf); the benchmark harness ships with the package (`qector bench`, `qector-doctor`).
